q: In what year was the White Paper published?
why: The 1966 White Paper started modern EMS after too many trauma deaths.

q: Name the four EMS levels.
a: emergency medical responder, EMT, AEMT, paramedic
why: EMR, EMT, AEMT, paramedic.

q: About how many hours of training is EMT?
why: EMT is about 130 to 150 hours of BLS and a short med list.

q: Whose license do you and the paramedic work under?
why: That doctor is legally responsible.

q: Who do you protect first on scene?
why: You first. If you become a patient, you help nobody.

q: What is the safety order on scene?
why: You first, then crew, then the patient.

q: In what order do you put PPE on?
a: clean hands, gown, mask, eyes, gloves
why: On: clean hands, gown, mask, eyes, gloves.

q: How far do you park from a fire, crash, or hazmat?
why: Park 100 feet from fires, crashes, hazmat.

q: Name the four pieces of negligence.
why: Negligence needs all four: duty, breach, damages, causation.

q: What is the first thing you do with an AED?
why: Turn the AED on and follow the voice prompts.

q: What adult compression depth?
why: Adult depth is at least 2 inches (5 cm). Allow full recoil.

q: What compression rate?
why: Rate 100–120 per minute. Not just at least 100.

q: You are the only one doing CPR. What ratio?
why: Single rescuer is 30:2 for every age.

q: An ICD fires. Can you touch them?
why: The jolt is low and internal. You can touch them when it fires.

q: An external defibrillator vest is shocking. What do you do with your hands?
why: The vest is a high-energy external shock. Do not touch while it shocks.

q: VAD patient, no pulse, talking. Are they perfusing?
why: Many VADs are continuous flow. If they are talking, they are perfusing.

q: Unconscious VAD patient. Who do you call?
why: Call the phone number on the controller and follow that team.

q: A pacemaker fails in the field. Can you fix it?
why: You cannot fix the pacemaker. Treat the slow rhythm and shock.

q: You ask them to smile on a stroke exam. What are you looking for?
why: Face: smile and look for droop.

q: Arms out, palms up, eyes closed. What finding means weakness?
why: One arm drifting down suggests weakness on that side.

q: What is last known well?
a: last time they were seen normal
the last time anyone saw them normal
why: Last known well is the last time anyone saw them normal.

q: About what percent of strokes are ischemic clots?
why: About 87 percent are ischemic. About 13 percent are hemorrhagic.

q: Do you give aspirin for suspected stroke?
why: Do not give aspirin for stroke. Aspirin in this recap is for suspected cardiac chest pain.

q: Stroke-like patient. What must you check before you lock in stroke?
why: Hypoglycemia can look exactly like a stroke. Check sugar first.

q: Where is classic appendicitis pain?
why: The appendix sits near the start of the colon in the right lower quadrant.

q: Kidney stones are usually made of what?
why: Stones are usually calcium, not too much fluid.
